title: Escape velocity and gravitational potential energy
log: 2026-10-27T00:53:13Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Escape velocity and gravitational potential energy
card: Gravitational potential energy between two masses is U = -GMm/r, where r is the distance between their centres. It is zero at infinite distance and negative everywhere closer.
Moving a mass away from a planet raises U towards zero, so work must be done on it. Moving closer lowers U, making it more negative.
Escape velocity is the launch speed needed to leave a planet's gravity with no further thrust. The object must reach infinity with at least zero kinetic energy.
So the starting kinetic energy must cancel the negative U: ½mv² = GMm/r. This gives v = √(2GM/r). The mass m cancels, so escape velocity does not depend on the mass of the object.
draft.remember: U is negative and rises to zero at infinity. Escape speed is the launch speed that makes total energy zero.

a.q: A rocket moves from the Earth's surface to a point far above it. What happens to its gravitational potential energy U?
opts: It stays the same, as U is always zero
It increases, becoming more positive than zero
a.why: U = -GMm/r, so a larger r gives a smaller negative number, which is a higher value. U rises towards zero but never passes it. The idea that U gets more negative with height mixes up the sign with the size of the number.
a.clue: Think about what happens to -GMm/r as r gets very large.

b.q: Two probes leave the same planet. Probe X has mass 200 kg and probe Y has mass 800 kg. What can be said about the escape velocity of each?
opts: They are the same, as mass cancels out
Y needs a higher speed, as it is heavier
X needs a higher speed, as it has less inertia
Y needs a lower speed, as gravity pulls it harder
b.why: Setting ½mv² = GMm/r cancels m, leaving v = √(2GM/r). Only the planet's mass and the starting distance matter. A heavier probe needs more energy in total, but not more speed.
b.clue: Look at what happens to m when kinetic energy is set equal to GMm/r.

b.best: They are the same, as mass cancels out
